title: Considerations for the Use of AI To Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products
text: Docket Number: FDA-2024-D-4689. This guidance provides recommendations to sponsors and other interested parties on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to produce information or data intended to support regulatory decision-making regarding safety, effectiveness, or quality for drugs. Specifically, this guidance provides a risk-based credibility assessment framework that may be used for establishing and evaluating the credibility of an AI model for a particular context of use (COU). You can submit online or written comments on any guidance at any time. All written comments should be identified with this document's docket number: FDA-2024-D-4689.

title: Conducting Clinical Trials With Decentralized Elements - Final Guidance (September 2024)
text: Final Level 1 Guidance. Docket Number: FDA-2022-D-2870. This guidance provides recommendations for sponsors, investigators, and other interested parties regarding the implementation of decentralized elements in clinical trials. Decentralized elements allow trial-related activities to occur remotely at locations convenient for trial participants. Decentralized elements can include, among other things, telehealth visits with trial personnel, in-home visits with remote trial personnel, or visits with local health care providers. In this guidance, a decentralized clinical trial refers to a clinical trial that includes decentralized elements where trial-related activities occur at locations other than traditional clinical trial sites.

title: Decentralized Clinical Trials for Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices; Draft Guidance; Availability
text: A Notice by the Food and Drug Administration on 05/03/2023. Published Document: 2023-09399 (88 FR 27900). Docket No. FDA-2022-D-2870. The FDA is announcing the availability of a draft guidance for industry, investigators, and other stakeholders entitled 'Decentralized Clinical Trials for Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices.' Submit either electronic or written comments on the draft guidance by August 1, 2023. In fully decentralized clinical trials, all activities take place at locations other than traditional trial sites. The investigator in a DCT is responsible for the conduct of the DCT and oversight of individuals delegated to perform trial-related activities. This draft guidance fulfills the requirements set forth in section 3606(a)(1) of the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act (FDORA).

title: Guiding Principles of Good AI Practice in Drug Development (January 2026)
text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to transform the way drugs are developed and evaluated, ultimately improving health care. In this context, AI refers to system-level technologies used to generate or analyze evidence across the drug product life cycle, including nonclinical, clinical, post-marketing, and manufacturing phases. The use of AI throughout the drug product life cycle has increased significantly in recent years. AI technologies are anticipated to support a multi-faceted approach that promotes innovation, reduces time-to-market, strengthens regulatory excellence and pharmacovigilance, and decreases reliance on animal testing by improving the prediction of toxicity and efficacy in humans. This document outlines a common set of principles to inform, enhance, and promote the use of AI for generating evidence across all phases of the drug product life cycle. These 10 guiding principles identify areas where international regulators, international standards organizations, and other collaborative bodies could work to advance good practice in drug development.

title: Amending OTC Monograph M012: Cold, Cough, Allergy, Bronchodilator, and Antiasthmatic Drug Products - Proposed Order
text: Docket No. FDA-2024-N-4734. The FDA is announcing the availability of the proposed administrative order (proposed order) (OTC000036) entitled 'Amending Over-the-Counter Monograph M012.' This proposed order, if finalized, will amend Final Administrative Order OTC000026, to remove orally administered phenylephrine hydrochloride and phenylephrine bitartrate in an effervescent dosage as nasal decongestant active ingredients because they are not effective. The electronic filing system will accept comments until 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time at the end of May 7, 2025. Comments must be submitted electronically to the Federal eRulemaking Portal at regulations.gov.

title: Warning Letter: Zydus Lifesciences Limited (06/02/2026)
text: This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. Because your methods, facilities, or controls do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B). 1. Your firm failed to withhold from use each lot of components until the lot had been sampled and tested, and failed to test samples for conformity with specifications (21 CFR 211.84): you have not demonstrated that you appropriately tested incoming talc for absence of asbestos to current USP requirements. 2. Your quality control unit failed to exercise its responsibility (21 CFR 211.22): an out-of-specification wavenumber result was removed from an infrared instrument report and multiple passing wavenumbers were added, allowing a failing identification test to appear as if it met release specifications. Between 2022 and 2025, out of 29 approved analytical results, 21 reports have identical maxima across different lots and dates, raising concerns regarding the authenticity of the reported results.

title: Warning Letter: Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited (07/28/2023)
text: This warning letter summarizes significant violations of current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. Your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B). 1. Your firm's quality control unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products are in compliance with CGMP (21 CFR 211.22): our inspection revealed serious deviations, including inadequate oversight of original CGMP documents, deficient controls over computerized systems, insufficient laboratory investigations, and aborted chromatographic sequences. Senior facility managers failed to exercise their authority to ensure reliable data. 2. Your firm failed to ensure laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests (21 CFR 211.194(a)). 3. Your firm failed to establish and follow required laboratory control mechanisms. Provide a comprehensive, independent assessment and CAPA plan for computer system security and integrity, including a list of all hardware and software, identification of vulnerabilities, and your remediated program for ensuring strict ongoing control over electronic and paper-based data.

title: Warning Letter: Fareva Amboise (04/10/2026)
text: This warning letter summarizes significant violations of FDA's Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations. Your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B). 3. Your firm failed to exercise appropriate controls over computer or related systems to assure that only authorized personnel institute changes in master production and control records, and you do not maintain a backup file of data (21 CFR 211.68(b)). Your systems do not have appropriate controls to prevent data deletion and record modifications. During the inspection, our investigator observed that operators could modify system dates, adjust alarm limits, and access settings without restriction. Review of electronic data stored on your particle counters revealed multiple instances where Grade A action limits for particle counts were exceeded; initial failing particle count results were not recorded in batch records. Instead, retests were performed, and only conforming retest results were retained. Your firm's vendor performed a calibration activity which deleted all electronic data prior to the calibration. You did not have backups of this data.

title: Warning Letter: Genzyme Ireland Limited (06/22/2026)
text: WARNING LETTER, June 22, 2026. FDA inspected your facility between January 12, 2026 and January 20, 2026 and documented evidence of significant violations of current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements in the manufacture of your licensed biological products, Thymoglobulin and Altuviiio. Your products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B). At the conclusion of the inspection, FDA investigators issued a Form FDA-483. 1. Your firm's quality control unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products are manufactured in compliance with CGMP: multiple non-viable particulate excursions and repeated test failures across multiple batches were not documented in laboratory records; testing was repeated up to 11 times without documentation. Additionally, your firm cancelled numerous deviations without investigating the root cause or assessing product impact. Although your retrospective review identified 36 deviations requiring further investigation, you did not provide sufficient justification limiting the review to the selected timeframe.

title: Warning Letter: Strides Pharma Science Limited (07/01/2019)
text: This warning letter summarizes significant violations of current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. 1. Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality control unit (21 CFR 211.22(a)): our investigator observed discarded CGMP documents and evidence of uncontrolled shredding of documents, including a blue binder containing CGMP records such as batch records for U.S. drug products discarded with other records in a 55-gallon drum in your scrap yard. CGMP documents in the binder were dated as recently as seven days before our inspection. 2. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch to meet specifications (21 CFR 211.192): your investigations of out-of-specification results were closed without adequate scientific justification. You identified an 'old reagent' as a root cause despite your inability to reproduce the unknown impurity, then retested a new sample and used the passing results to release the API. Until you correct all violations completely, FDA may withhold approval of any new applications listing your firm as a drug manufacturer.

title: FDA warns of rare but serious drug reaction (DRESS) to antiseizure medicines levetiracetam and clobazam
text: FDA is warning that the antiseizure medicines levetiracetam (Keppra, Keppra XR, Elepsia XR, Spritam) and clobazam (Onfi, Sympazan) can cause a rare but serious reaction that can be life-threatening if not diagnosed and treated quickly. This reaction is called Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS). It may start as a rash but can quickly progress, resulting in injury to internal organs, the need for hospitalization, and even death. We are requiring warnings about this risk to be added to the prescribing information and patient Medication Guides. FDA's cumulative review found serious cases of DRESS worldwide (32 for levetiracetam and 10 for clobazam); most patients required hospitalization and two patients treated with levetiracetam died. The median time to onset was 24 days.

title: Prolia (denosumab): FDA Adds Boxed Warning for Increased Risk of Severe Hypocalcemia in Patients with Advanced CKD
text: ISSUE: Based on a completed FDA review of available information, FDA has concluded that the osteoporosis medicine Prolia (denosumab) increases the risk of severe hypocalcemia, very low blood calcium levels, in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly patients on dialysis. In patients with advanced CKD taking Prolia, severe hypocalcemia resulted in serious harm, including hospitalization, life-threatening events, and death. As a result, the FDA is revising the Prolia prescribing information to include a new Boxed Warning, FDA's most prominent warning. Severe hypocalcemia can be asymptomatic or may present with symptoms that include confusion; seizures; irregular heart rhythm; fainting; face twitching; uncontrolled muscle spasms; or weakness, tingling, or numbness. The FDA is adding this updated information to the patient Medication Guide and the Prolia Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS).

title: FDA requires Boxed Warning about serious mental health side effects for montelukast (Singulair)
text: What safety concern is FDA announcing? The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is strengthening existing warnings about serious behavior and mood-related changes with montelukast (Singulair and generics), a prescription medicine for asthma and allergy. We are taking this action after a review of available information led us to reevaluate the benefits and risks of montelukast use. Montelukast prescribing information already includes warnings about mental health side effects, including suicidal thoughts or actions; however, many health care professionals and patients/caregivers are not aware of the risk. We are requiring a Boxed Warning, our most prominent warning, to be added to the prescribing information of montelukast to describe these serious mental health side effects and to recommend that montelukast should only be reserved to treat allergic rhinitis in patients who are not treated effectively with or cannot tolerate other allergy medicines. We are also requiring a new patient Medication Guide.

title: FDA requires warnings about increased risk of serious heart-related events, cancer, blood clots, and death for JAK inhibitors
text: Based on a completed FDA review of a large randomized safety clinical trial, we have concluded there is an increased risk of serious heart-related events such as heart attack or stroke, cancer, blood clots, and death with the arthritis and ulcerative colitis medicines Xeljanz and Xeljanz XR (tofacitinib). The trial's final results also showed an increased risk of blood clots and death with the lower dose of Xeljanz. We are requiring new and updated warnings for two other medicines in the same drug class, Olumiant (baricitinib) and Rinvoq (upadacitinib). We are requiring revisions to the Boxed Warning for Xeljanz/Xeljanz XR, Olumiant, and Rinvoq. In addition, to ensure the benefits of these medicines outweigh the risks, we are limiting all approved uses to certain patients who have not responded or cannot tolerate one or more TNF blockers. Changes will also be made to several sections of the prescribing information and to the patient Medication Guide.

title: FDA Adds Boxed Warning to Labeling for Ferric Carboxymaltose Injection (Injectafer) for Risk of Low Phosphate Levels
text: FDA Drug Safety Communication - September 1, 2026. The FDA has approved revisions to the labeling for ferric carboxymaltose injection (marketed as Injectafer) that adds a boxed warning describing the risk for symptomatic hypophosphatemia associated with ferric carboxymaltose injection and recommends phosphate monitoring in patients at risk. In 2026, FDA conducted an assessment of hypophosphatemia using multiple data sources, including the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database, literature reports, and FDA's Sentinel System. FDA found that symptomatic hypophosphatemia continues to be reported and serum phosphate testing levels are low despite labeling changes in February 2020 and May 2023. Hypophosphatemia associated with ferric carboxymaltose can lead to serious outcomes including hospitalization, a need for prolonged phosphate replacement therapy, osteomalacia, and fractures. This serious adverse reaction can be prevented or reduced in severity through appropriate phosphate level monitoring and early intervention.

title: Comparative Cardiovascular Pharmacovigilance of Semaglutide and Tirzepatide: A FAERS Database Analysis (2022-2026)
text: BACKGROUND: Semaglutide and tirzepatide are primary treatments for cardiometabolic disease, yet their comparative real-world cardiovascular safety requires further characterization. OBJECTIVE: To conduct a pharmacovigilance disproportionality analysis comparing cardiovascular adverse event signals between semaglutide and tirzepatide utilizing FAERS data from January 2022 to March 2026. METHODS: Cardiac AEs were extracted from the FAERS database. Disproportionality was evaluated using reporting odds ratios (RORs) and proportional reporting ratios (PRRs). RESULTS: Analysis included 56,799 semaglutide and 135,992 tirzepatide reports. Overall, cardiac AE reporting was disproportionately favorable to semaglutide (ROR: 2.85). Semaglutide exhibited significant signals in eight of 12 cardiac categories, notably congestive heart failure (ROR: 8.09), cardiac failure (3.69), cardiac arrest (3.42), and atrial fibrillation (3.37). Fatal outcomes also favored semaglutide (ROR: 3.14). CONCLUSIONS: These findings likely reflect underlying demographic and indication-based risk differences rather than direct toxicity.

title: Comparison of cardiac adverse event signal profiles for GLP-1 receptor agonists: an analysis of the FAERS database
text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are widely used in the management of type 2 diabetes owing to their effectiveness in glycemic control and weight reduction. Given the increasing use of GLP-1RAs, further research is warranted to better understand their cardiac effects. Individual Case Safety Reports from the FAERS database from July 6, 2007 to February 17, 2026 were evaluated for the post-marketing cardiac adverse events associated with dulaglutide, liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide. A total of 7,023 cardiac adverse events were identified among 305,877 reports. GLP-1RAs were associated with a higher reporting frequency of tachyarrhythmias than bradyarrhythmias. In the 65-85-year age group, an increase in the signal for cardiac events was observed. Semaglutide and liraglutide had higher relative reporting of cardiac events whereas tirzepatide had lower PRR and ROR values. These findings suggest a lower reporting tendency of cardiac events for tirzepatide.

title: Mortality and Serious Adverse Events Associated With GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: A FAERS Pharmacovigilance Study
text: Postmarket surveillance is essential for characterizing risk profiles of GLP-1RAs in real-world patient populations as clinical use increases. A disproportionality analysis was conducted utilizing FAERS data from Q2 2005 to Q1 2024 to identify AEs listing an approved GLP-1RA as the primary suspect drug. The analysis identified 287,201 AEs associated with GLP-1RAs. Disproportionality analyses revealed statistically significant elevated signals for mortality with the earliest approved GLP-1RAs: Byetta (ROR = 2.20) and Victoza (ROR = 2.12). Significant elevated signals for serious AEs were identified with the semaglutide products Ozempic (ROR = 2.77), Rybelsus (2.42), and Wegovy (1.30); the liraglutide products Victoza (2.10) and Saxenda (2.21); and Byetta (1.11). The newer GLP-1RAs were associated with a higher proportion of serious AEs reported in younger patients and females. These findings highlight the importance of proactive postmarket surveillance and of individually evaluating drugs within the same pharmacological class.

title: Postmarketing Safety Signals and Medication-Use Risks of GLP-1-Based Therapies: Multi-Source Pharmacovigilance Evidence-Mapping Study
text: AIMS: To characterise postmarketing safety signals and medication-use risks associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists and the GIP/GLP-1 co-agonist tirzepatide in diabetes and obesity care using an integrated pharmacovigilance, utilisation-context, regulatory, and external-consistency framework. METHODS: FAERS data from 2021Q1 through 2026Q1 were processed using deleted-case exclusion, latest-case-version retention, and case-product deduplication. Primary-suspect records for semaglutide, tirzepatide, dulaglutide, liraglutide, exenatide, and lixisenatide were analysed using reporting odds ratios, proportional reporting ratios, and an approximate Information Component. The final analysis set included 243,114 GLP-1 primary-suspect case-product records within 8,995,547 background reports. Frequently reported terms included incorrect dose administered, nausea, injection-site pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, off-label use, and extra dose administered. CONCLUSIONS: Findings should be interpreted as signal-prioritisation and medication-safety evidence, not as incidence, proof of causality, or population-level comparative risk.

title: What we have learned from trying to remove oral phenylephrine from the market
text: A 2023 United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Nonprescription Drug Advisory Committee unanimously voted that oral phenylephrine is not Generally Recognized As Safe and Effective (GRASE). This decision resulted, in part, from our nearly 20 years as clinical pharmacists advocating for patients with nasal congestion. In this article, we describe the role of a Freedom of Information request for unpublished data, our systematic review and meta-analysis of the data upon which the FDA relied to approve oral phenylephrine, our two Citizen Petitions, and modern data, including an unpublished study from clinicaltrials.gov. The FDA recently posted a proposal to remove oral phenylephrine from the market, and the American College of Clinical Pharmacy (ACCP) has been a key stakeholder supporting the removal.

title: Citizen's Petition to remove oral phenylephrine from the Final Monograph for OTC nasal decongestant products
text: The undersigned submit this petition under 21 CFR Part 10.30 to request the Commissioner of Food and Drugs to remove oral phenylephrine from the Final Monograph for OTC nasal decongestant products. A. Action Requested: To issue a final rule removing oral phenylephrine from the Final Monograph. B. Statement of Grounds: On February 6, 2007, we submitted a Citizen's Petition to FDA requesting that the dosage of oral phenylephrine be re-evaluated. The basis of the request was our systematic review and meta-analysis of the studies considered by the agency. The agency convened its Nonprescription Drugs Advisory Committee on December 14, 2007, and nine of the 12 committee members voted that new studies on response to higher doses were required. Schering-Plough conducted a multicenter, phase 2, parallel trial among 539 adults with seasonal allergic rhinitis. There were no significant differences between placebo and active treatment groups. The results of the 4 studies reported after the 2007 Advisory Committee Meeting clearly demonstrate that PE is no more effective than placebo.

title: Dompé U.S. Agrees to Pay $32M to Resolve False Claims Act Liability Relating to Self-Disclosure of Patient Kickbacks
text: For Immediate Release, Thursday, September 10, 2026. Dompé U.S. Inc. has agreed to pay $32 million to resolve allegations that, between 2018 and 2021, it paid Medicare beneficiary co-pays through two patient assistance foundations to induce the purchase of its drug, Oxervate, in violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute and the False Claims Act. 'This settlement demonstrates the United States' commitment to enforcing the Anti-Kickback Statute and ensuring that pharmaceutical manufacturers do not use unlawful inducements,' said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate. Dompé admitted that, around the time of Oxervate's 2018 launch, employees expressed reservations about launching the drug before making a payment to a patient assistance foundation. Dompé farmaceutici self-disclosed this conduct to the United States and received credit under the Department's guidelines for self-disclosure, cooperation, and remediation. The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only.

title: Veloxis Pharmaceuticals Agrees to Pay Over $46M to Resolve Criminal and Civil Liability for Kickback Schemes
text: Monday, August 10, 2026. Veloxis Pharmaceuticals Inc. has agreed to pay over $46 million to resolve criminal and civil allegations that it paid kickbacks to induce prescriptions and purchases of Envarsus XR, a kidney transplant immunosuppression drug. The company entered into a deferred prosecution agreement in connection with a criminal information charging conspiracy to commit violations of the federal Anti-Kickback Statute by paying for lavish meals, alcohol, and luxury resort stays to induce healthcare providers to prescribe Envarsus. Veloxis also agreed to pay a $1.55 million civil penalty to CMS to resolve allegations that it knowingly failed to report certain payments to physicians under the Open Payments Program (Sunshine Act) - the largest Sunshine Act recovery since the law was passed in 2010. Veloxis entered into a five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement with HHS-OIG. The claims include allegations brought under the qui tam or whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act.

title: Pfizer Agrees to Pay Nearly $60M to Resolve False Claims Allegations Relating to Improper Physician Payments by Subsidiary
text: Pharmaceutical company Pfizer Inc., on behalf of its wholly-owned subsidiary Biohaven Pharmaceutical Holding Company Ltd., has agreed to pay $59,746,277 to resolve allegations that, prior to Pfizer's acquisition, Biohaven knowingly caused the submission of false claims to Medicare and other federal health care programs by paying kickbacks to health care providers to induce prescriptions of Biohaven's drug Nurtec ODT. The settlement resolves allegations that from March 1, 2020, through September 30, 2022, Biohaven paid improper remuneration, including speaker honoraria and meals at high end restaurants, to health care professionals to induce them to prescribe the migraine medication. Certain prescribers who attended multiple programs on the same topic received no educational benefit, and certain speaker programs were attended by individuals with no educational need, such as the speakers' spouses, family members, or friends. The civil settlement includes resolution of claims brought under the qui tam provisions by a former sales representative.

title: Drug Maker Teva Pharmaceuticals Agrees to Pay $450M to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations and Kickback Claims
text: The U.S. Department of Justice announced that Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc. agreed to pay $450 million to resolve alleged False Claims Act liability for kickback schemes and tainted salary payments related to blockbuster drugs, including Copaxone. The resolution includes allegations that Teva paid kickbacks in the form of speaker and advisory fees, honoraria, and meals to physicians to induce them to prescribe Teva drugs, and that a Teva employee, while on the company payroll, simultaneously served as a specialty pharmacy's clinical director, receiving salary from both companies while influencing formulary decisions that benefited Teva. The settlement resolves a qui tam lawsuit under the whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act. Note to reviewers: this excerpt was reconstructed from the DOJ announcement headline and case summary because the archived page served an anti-bot shell to automated fetchers; verify at the source URL before external use.

title: FDA green lights Priovant drug for rare skin disease
text: The Food and Drug Administration on Thursday cleared the first oral therapy for a rare and debilitating skin condition. Called brepocitinib and to be sold as Lisraya, the drug was originally discovered by Pfizer and licensed to Priovant Therapeutics, a subsidiary of Roivant Sciences. It's been cleared for use treating dermatomyositis, a condition that causes muscle weakness and skin lesions. A 30-day supply will have a list price of $35,000, executives revealed on a Friday conference call. 'For too long, patients with dermatomyositis have faced a significant unmet need for effective treatments,' said Nikolay Nikolov, the director of the FDA office that evaluates immunology and inflammation drugs. The most common side effects included infection, headache, fatigue, nausea and diarrhea. The drug's prescribing information carries the same kind of 'boxed warning' as other JAK blockers.

title: Fresenius pulls one batch of Actemra biosimilar over glass particle concerns
text: Fresenius Kabi is yanking a batch of another product in the U.S., shortly after initiating a separate recall tied to mislabeled pain medicine. Fresenius has issued a recall of its biosimilar Tyenne (tocilizumab-aazg) injection in 20 ml vials, after a company investigation found the product contained glass particles. Injecting medication with glass particles can cause irritation, pain or swelling at the infusion site, as well as potential inflammation of the veins, Fresenius said in a recall notice posted on the FDA's website. As of Aug. 12, Fresenius Kabi had not received any adverse event reports tied to the recall. Tyenne is a biosimilar referencing Roche's IL-6 receptor antagonist Actemra. Fresenius' recall covers a single lot of Tyenne, which was distributed across the U.S. In 2024, Gilead recalled one batch of Veklury after detecting a glass particle in a vial, and the issue also led to similar product pulls for GSK and Pfizer the year before.

title: Fresenius unit dinged in FDA warning letter flagging 'complaint trend' from customers
text: Following a string of customer complaints, a Form 483 and a recall this past spring, a Fresenius manufacturing unit in Utah is contending with a warning letter from the FDA. The FDA reprimand, dated Aug. 25, follows an inspection of Fresenius Medical Care's plant in Ogden, Utah, in early March. In two observations, the FDA's concerns focused on the company's failure to thoroughly investigate customer complaints about its products, plus lackluster inspection protocols at the plant to suss out potential particulate contamination. Last August, the Fresenius unit kicked off its own investigation due to a 'complaint trend' around 'leaking bags' of a dialysis solution product, eventually receiving 35 complaints related to some 156 bags. The company launched a related recall this past April, but the FDA chided that it 'chose not to conduct a recall following the results of your August 2025 investigation.' 'Your decision not to recall these batches at that time exposed peritoneal dialysis patients to potentially non-sterile drug products,' the regulator continued.

title: FDA places partial hold on Biohaven's epilepsy drug
text: Biohaven shares fell by more than 10% Thursday after the company revealed that the FDA has placed a partial hold on an experimental epilepsy medicine it recently sold off rights to in a licensing deal. In a regulatory filing, Biohaven disclosed that the FDA has requested additional data related to a 'metabolite,' or drug-related substance, that was identified in rodent studies of its treatment opakalim. The agency instructed Biohaven to pause recruitment in an ongoing late-stage trial until it can provide more information. Dosing will continue for those already involved in that study, 'RISE-2.' Importantly, the hold doesn't affect a separate late-stage trial, 'RISE-3,' that's fully enrolled. That study is still expected to produce results later this year. The pause in RISE-2 enrollment delays a readout that could be 'ultimately necessary for an approval,' wrote RBC Capital Markets analyst Leonid Timashev.

title: Biohaven takes another hit as FDA pauses enrollment in pivotal trials for embattled epilepsy drug
text: Biohaven stock fell more than 13% in premarket trading Thursday as the FDA slapped a partial clinical hold on its Kv7 potassium channel agonist in focal epilepsy. The enrollment pause comes after BHV-7000 failed to show efficacy in a midstage depression trial late last year, and is another regulatory hit after the FDA declined to approve its spinocerebellar ataxia treatment in November 2025. The partial hold pertains to the enrollment of new patients in two late-stage focal epilepsy studies. It was placed so the FDA could assess potential risk to humans from a metabolite identified during rodent testing, according to a Thursday SEC filing. Dosing will continue for all patients already randomized in the two pivotal trials - RISE 2 and RISE 3 - which together comprise more than 600 participants. RISE 2 was previously expected to have a primary completion date in December this year.

title: Veeva Falcon Safety to Work with All E2B-Compliant Safety Systems Across Any Intake Channels
text: PLEASANTON, Calif., Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Veeva Systems today announced Veeva Falcon Safety, an agentic safety operations product to streamline adverse event intake, case processing, and follow-up to reduce costs, increase speed, and maintain compliance for biopharma companies of all sizes. In addition to working seamlessly with Veeva Safety, Falcon Safety will provide intake and follow-up management for any E2B-compliant safety system, including Oracle Argus and ArisGlobal LifeSphere MultiVigilance. 'With Falcon Safety, we're excited to build on that partnership to help the industry reinvent safety operations,' said Marius Mortensen, vice president of product, Falcon at Veeva. Planned for early adopter availability in November 2026, Falcon Safety is part of Veeva AI, Veeva's industry-specific AI solutions for life sciences. Veeva serves more than 1,500 customers, ranging from the world's largest pharmaceutical companies to emerging biotechs.

title: Veeva Introduces Falcon Router for Agentic Triage of All Reporting Channels
text: PLEASANTON, Calif., Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Veeva Systems today announced Veeva Falcon Router, an industry-specific agent to identify and route potential safety adverse event reports, product quality complaints, and medical inquiries to the correct teams with speed and consistency. Falcon Router will orchestrate triage and routing actions for biopharmas of all sizes, without the need for manual reconciliation. The initial focus will be on email and web intake, including Veeva Ostro. Falcon Router will route triaged information directly to Veeva Safety, Veeva QMS, Veeva MedInquiry, or designated inboxes. 'Every biopharma faces this routing challenge, and it grows with every new region and product they bring to market,' said John Lawrie, vice president, Veeva Safety. 'Fast, reliable triage is more important than ever so that experts can focus on what matters most, the patient.' Planned for early adopter availability in January 2027.

title: BioDlink Modernizes Quality Management with Successful Go-Live of Veeva QMS
text: SUZHOU, China, Feb. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BioDlink today announced the successful go-live of Veeva QMS, marking a key milestone in the company's quality digitalization strategy. The initial deployment covers four core quality processes: Deviation Management, Change Management, Laboratory Investigation, and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Management. Additional modules, including Quality Risk Management, Audit Management, Supplier Management, Annual Product Quality Review, and Management Review, are planned for future phases. BioDlink, a leading global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) specializing in biologics, delivers end-to-end CDMO services for protein-based therapeutics, biosimilar, and bioconjugated drugs from early-stage research through to commercial-scale manufacturing. Veeva QMS is a cloud-based quality management system purpose-built for the life sciences industry; more than 300 companies worldwide streamline quality processes with Veeva QMS, including 17 of the Top 20 global pharmas.

title: Veeva Quality Cloud Advances Manufacturing Operations for Kindeva
text: Global CDMO will unify sites on single quality platform for greater efficiency and scalability. PLEASANTON, Calif., May 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Veeva Systems today announced Kindeva is adopting Veeva Quality Cloud to modernize its manufacturing operations, bringing together its global network of sites onto a single cloud platform. With Veeva QualityDocs, Veeva QMS, Veeva Training, and Veeva LearnGxP, Kindeva is building a scalable technology foundation that can meet new customer requirements as the business continues its growth trajectory. 'Implementing Veeva Quality Cloud will enhance our quality management infrastructure to enable greater standardization, real-time visibility across operations, more efficient collaboration, and secure information exchange with our customers,' said Melanie Cerullo, chief quality officer at Kindeva. The contract development and manufacturing organization can operate more efficiently and eliminate data silos as it advances its fill-finish operations.

title: FDA approves Pharming's Joenja as first treatment for children with APDS in the U.S.
text: Leiden, the Netherlands, September 11, 2026: Pharming, a global biotechnology company focused on rare immune and genetic diseases, today announced that the FDA has approved its supplemental New Drug Application for 40 mg and 50 mg twice-daily dosing of Joenja (leniolisib), an oral, selective PI3Kdelta inhibitor, as a treatment for children aged 4 to 11 years with activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS), a rare primary immunodeficiency. With this approval, Joenja becomes the first FDA-approved treatment for children aged 4 to 11 years with APDS in the U.S. The newly approved doses are expected to be available in October through Pharming's specialty distribution network and patient-support infrastructure. Today's approval is supported by data from a multinational, open-label, single-arm Phase III study demonstrating improvements over 12 weeks in reduced lymphadenopathy and increased naïve B cells. The safety profile was consistent with prior experience.

title: CSPI Comments on FDA's Proposed Order Regarding Removal of Oral Phenylephrine (Docket FDA-2024-N-4734)
text: May 6, 2025. Dockets Management Staff, FDA. Re: Amending Over-the-Counter Monograph M012 (Docket No. FDA-2024-N-4734-0001). The undersigned individuals write in strong support of the FDA's November 8, 2024, proposed order to remove the oral decongestant phenylephrine (PE) as a nasal decongestant active ingredient from OTC Monograph M012. Data provided to the agency show that oral PE is not effectively absorbed into the bloodstream. Dr. Leslie Hendeles and Dr. Randy Hatton have submitted two Citizen Petitions to the FDA on oral PE efficacy. Their 2007 Citizen Petition revealed that one study site (Elizabeth Biochemical Labs) drove the reported positive efficacy outcomes for PE, and that this site's results could not be replicated by other study sites. In September 2023, the FDA convened an NDAC meeting which voted unanimously that current scientific data do not support that the monograph dosage of orally administered phenylephrine is effective as a nasal decongestant.

title: Public Citizen Comments on the FDA's Proposed Order Regarding Removal of Oral Phenylephrine
text: May 7, 2025. Public Citizen submits the below comments in strong support of the FDA's notice of proposed administrative order OTC000036, which would remove orally administered phenylephrine hydrochloride and effervescent phenylephrine bitartrate as nasal-decongestant active ingredients from the OTC monograph because they are ineffective. We are deeply concerned that, for almost fifty years, the FDA has maintained the GRASE status of oral phenylephrine despite compelling research evidence against its effectiveness. Although there are no safety concerns for oral phenylephrine products, U.S. consumers would not be served by leaving such placebo-like products on the market. In 2007 a meta-analysis by University of Florida researchers evaluated eight unpublished efficacy studies for the 10-mg dose obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request; contrary to common assumptions, the meta-analysis did not find oral phenylephrine to be efficacious. In September 2023 an FDA Advisory Committee unanimously voted (16-0) that the current dosage is not effective for nasal congestion relief.

title: PhRMA Comments on FDA Draft Guidance: Considerations for the Use of AI to Support Regulatory Decision-Making (FDA-2024-D-4689)
text: April 7, 2025. Re: Docket No. FDA-2024-D-4689 - Considerations for the Use of Artificial Intelligence to Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products; Draft Guidance for Industry. The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is pleased to submit these comments in response to the FDA request for comments. PhRMA strongly agrees with FDA that advancements in AI hold the potential to accelerate the development of safe and effective drugs. FDA's risk-based credibility assessment framework is a welcomed step. PhRMA strongly believes that credibility assessment plans and reports for lower-risk model uses do not need to be submitted to the Agency, and recommends such a reflection in the Draft Guidance. PhRMA encourages FDA to explicitly address the application of the Credibility Framework to LLM-based tools and generative AI, since many recommendations pertaining to training and tuning data and confidence intervals would be challenging to fully meet for LLM-based AI models. PhRMA also encourages clarity that the Draft Guidance does not apply to previously reviewed uses of AI models.

title: BIO Comments Opposing the CMS Global Benchmark for Efficient Drug Pricing (GLOBE) Model (CMS-5545-P)
text: February 23, 2026. Re: Global Benchmark for Efficient Drug Pricing (GLOBE) Model (CMS-5545-P). The Biotechnology Innovation Organization (BIO) appreciates the opportunity to comment on the CMS GLOBE Model proposed rule. BIO strongly opposes GLOBE and urges the Administration to withdraw the Proposed Rule in its entirety. GLOBE would implement government price controls in Medicare, allowing foreign nations and non-U.S. companies to dictate pricing policies for U.S. pharmaceutical manufacturers. GLOBE violates numerous statutory boundaries on the authority of the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation, attempting to rewrite CMS's statutory authority in order to invent a new mandatory, nationwide, punitive price-setting framework. The proposal also violates numerous core constitutional and legal principles, including major questions doctrine, appropriations law, the Presentment, Due Process, and Takings clauses, and separation of powers. International reference pricing policies have resulted in reduced investment in biotech research and development and slower introduction of new therapies.

title: PhRMA Comments on CMS Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program Draft Guidance for IPAY 2028
text: Re: Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program: Draft Guidance, Implementation of Sections 1191-1198 of the Social Security Act for Initial Price Applicability Year 2028. PhRMA appreciates the opportunity to respond to the CMS draft guidance released on May 12, 2025. Yet 50 percent of medicine spending goes to someone who did not make the medicines. Growth in patient out-of-pocket costs has outpaced growth in the prices paid by insurers - price setting does not address these challenges. Nine in 10 Part D plans say they intend to increase access restrictions on medicines in the coming years because of the IRA. 3.5 million patients taking medicines subject to price setting may see higher out-of-pocket costs in 2026, with OOP costs climbing 12 percent on average. The IRA unconstitutionally delegates legislative power to CMS. PhRMA opposes the overbroad interpretation of a qualifying single source drug (QSSD) that CMS used for IPAY 2026 and 2027. Under Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo, an agency is required to apply the single, best meaning of a statute.

text: The following include some but not all of the factors that could cause actual results or events to differ from those anticipated: the significant costs and uncertainties in the pharmaceutical research and development process; continued pricing pressures and the impact of actions of governmental and private actors affecting pricing of, reimbursement for, and patient access to pharmaceuticals; negotiation and implementation of our voluntary agreement with the U.S. government related to drug pricing and access; developments or uncertainties related to our or competitive products, including as may relate to safety or efficacy concerns; dependence on relatively few products or product classes for a significant percentage of our total revenue; the expiration of intellectual property protection for certain of our products; the use of artificial intelligence or other emerging technologies in various facets of our operations, including partnerships related to the use of, or the sharing of, such technologies with third parties, which may exacerbate competitive, regulatory, litigation, cybersecurity, and other risks. title: Sarepta Therapeutics Form 10-K - Risk Factors Summary
text: Risk Factors Summary: We are highly dependent on the commercial success of our products in the U.S. Even though certain of our products have received accelerated approval from the FDA, they face future post-approval development and regulatory requirements. Our products or product candidates may cause undesirable side effects, result in new safety signals or have other properties that could delay or prevent regulatory approval, limit the commercial potential or result in significant negative consequences (including revocation) following any existing or potential marketing approval. Our announced strategic restructuring plan may not result in anticipated reductions in expenses. We are investing significant resources in the development of novel siRNA and gene therapy product candidates. Because we are developing product candidates for the treatment of certain diseases in which there is little clinical experience and we are using new endpoints or methodologies, the FDA, the EMA or other regulatory authorities may not consider the endpoints of our clinical trials to provide clinically meaningful results. text: Summary of Material Risks Associated with Our Business: our ability to maintain and grow commercial sales of our products depends on many factors, including the availability of adequate levels of reimbursement or increases in patients' financial obligation which could result in decreased sales; if there are changes in, or we fail to comply with, the extensive legal and regulatory requirements affecting the healthcare industry, we could be subject to investigations, litigation, costs, penalties and business losses; disruptions at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and other government agencies could negatively impact our business; LUMRYZ is a controlled substance subject to U.S. federal and state-controlled substance laws and regulations, and any failure to comply could materially adversely affect our business; risks from actions such as citizens petitions. text: Summary of Risk Factors: We may not be able to continue as a going concern.
